route: Realising the second blow-up level by hand: the inner game is given, the outer layer is a design problem (labels gad:)
headline: The second blow-up level IS realised: an explicit nondegenerate stopping SSG on 138 vertices (5 Max, 1 Min, 130 average, 2 sinks, denominator 2^9) whose improvement orientation is exactly B^2 = B(B(1-cube)), a 5-cube AUSO of bottom-antipodal height 10, verified from the game in exact arithmetic with the all-switches run of length 10 printed round by round. Four new obstruction theorems (gad:readout, gad:mono, gad:face, gad:precision) explain why every earlier search failed, say exactly where the Min vertex must act, and are what made the construction findable; the measured size recurrence from level 1 to level 2 is +2 Max, +1 Min, +3 bits, the additive regime.

results.name: gad:B2
results.statement: There is a nondegenerate stopping SSG on 138 vertices - five Max, one Min, 130 average and the two sinks - whose improvement outmap is exactly B^2 = B(B(1-cube)) = (7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6,24,9,27,14,31,28,29,10,16,25,19,30,23,20,21,26,8,17,11,22,15,12,13,18), an acyclic unique sink orientation of the 5-cube of bottom-antipodal height 10, whose all-switches run from sigma=12 has length 10: 12->19->13->17->8->16->0->7->1->5->4. Harmonic normal form, denominator 512, rows (p over c1..c6 | q on t1), the rest to t0:  c1:(12,461,36,0,0,0|0) (276,0,0,0,127,0|47); c2:(0,0,509,0,0,0|0) (0,83,0,0,320,0|12); c3:(0,0,0,0,0,460|43) (267,187,0,0,56,0|0); c4:(0,0,0,0,502,0|8) (71,293,23,0,0,0|0); c5:(0,0,0,509,0,0|0) (0,0,0,0,0,419|1); c6 (Min):(472,0,0,0,0,0|0) (0,493,0,0,16,0|1).
results.argument: Constructed. The twelve substochastic rows are realised by Knuth-Yao trees of fair coins (def:damping), giving the explicit game. This settles the instance that rem:blowup-measured named 'the smallest open instance' of the pivot, and prop:oneplayer-lp forces the Min vertex because the orientation is not Holt-Klee.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic throughout, twice and independently. (i) On the normal form (gcore.NFG): val_sigma computed for all 32 Max strategies as the componentwise MINIMUM over both positional Min strategies of the two pair values - never policy iteration - and checked to be a fixed point of T_sigma; all 160 incidences strict; outmap == B^2 exactly. (ii) On the built game (verify.analyse): greatest trap empty so stopping (lem:trapchar); every non-sink of out-degree two; 64 pair values cross-checked against a second independent elimination core; outmap recomputed from the game == B^2; nondegenerate, Szabo-Welzl on all C(32,2) pairs, acyclic by DFS; BA heights 4,2,4,3,0,1,2,3,6,5,8,2,10,8,10,2,5,7,3,9,4,3,4,9,6,7,8,9,10,8,10,9; Holt-Klee fails on the unit vertex-capacity max-flow test; val_sigma increases at every one of the 136 non-sink vertices at every round of the run. Files: B2_small_nf.json, B2_small_GAME.json; a second realisation at denominator 2^10 on 155 vertices in B2_155_nf.json / B2_155_game.json.

results.name: gad:readout
results.statement: Let x_i be a Max vertex with reduced (self-return-eliminated) rows A_i, B_i, i.e. p-hat^{i,a}_u = p^{i,a}_u/(1-p^{i,a}_i). Then val_sigma(x_i) = A_i(y) when sigma_i=0 and B_i(y) when sigma_i=1, where y = val_sigma off x_i, and sign Delta_i(val_sigma) = sign(B_i(y)-A_i(y)). Hence val_sigma(x_i) takes three levels relative to A_i(y): equal when sigma_i=0, above when sigma_i=1 and i is not switchable, below when sigma_i=1 and i is switchable.
results.argument: val_sigma(x_i) is the fixed point of t -> p^{i,sigma_i}_i t + (rest), which is A_i(y) or B_i(y) since p_i<1 for a stopping game; substituting gives Delta_i = (1-p^{i,1-sigma_i}_i)(B_i(y)-A_i(y)) with a positive prefactor in both cases. This is the reason the state of a Max vertex is visible in the value vector only through the conjunction of sigma_i with its own incidence - the exact content of rem:blowup-realise's 'the state of j reaches the rest of the game only through val(j)'.
results.verification: Algebraic; and the three-level structure is exhibited exactly on the realised B(2-cube) game (gad:xor).

results.name: gad:mono / gad:B2-rows
results.statement: If the reduced rows of x_i are comparable (p-hat^{i,1} >= p-hat^{i,0} and q-hat^{i,1} >= q-hat^{i,0}) then {sigma : g_i(sigma)=+} is up-closed in the reachability preorder of the improvement orientation; with the reverse inequalities, down-closed. Consequently, in EVERY nondegenerate stopping realisation of B^2 the two reduced rows of each of the five Max vertices are incomparable; in particular no Max vertex may have an action that goes straight to the sinks, nor one that returns only to itself and the sinks. For B^1 only beta_1 needs incomparable rows.
results.argument: By gad:readout, g_i is the sign of the affine functional B_i - A_i, whose coefficient vector is p-hat^{i,1}-p-hat^{i,0}; and val_sigma is nondecreasing along every directed edge of the orientation (lem:switch). For B^2 the outmap contains, for each coordinate, a directed edge on which g goes + -> - and another on which it goes - -> +; witnesses (as vertex pairs of the 5-cube, coordinates x,alpha_1,beta_1,alpha_2,beta_2 = bits 0..4): x: 0->4 and 8->0; alpha_1: 0->1 and 8->0; beta_1: 2->3 and 3->1; alpha_2: 17->16 and 18->19; beta_2: 8->0 and 9->8.
results.verification: Finite enumeration over the outmap (mono.py), cross-checked against the realised games: the found 138-vertex realisation indeed has all five row pairs incomparable, and the realised B(2-cube) game does pin its translated coordinate by a pure self-return, exactly as the corollary permits at level one and forbids at level two.

results.name: gad:face (the crossing lemma)
results.statement: Let G be nondegenerate stopping and F a 2-face of the Max cube spanned by coordinates i,j whose four Max strategies have a common optimal Min response. Then (a) the four value vectors lie in an affine 2-plane; (b) the segment joining the two values with sigma_i=0 and the segment joining the two with sigma_i=1 meet if and only if g_i is non-constant on F; (c) at most one of g_i,g_j is non-constant (unique-sink axiom), and if it is g_i then NO affine functional of the value vector separates F by sigma_i.
results.argument: (a) val_sigma is the unique solution of the |C| equations z_v = V_v^{sigma_v}(z), z_y = V_y^{tau_y}(z); |C| hyperplanes with a unique common point are independent, so the |C|-2 shared ones meet in a plane of dimension exactly 2. (b) with phi_0 = z_i - V_i^0, phi_1 = z_i - V_i^1 and Delta_i = phi_0 - phi_1: neither phi is constant on the plane (else Delta_i vanishes at two points, against nondegeneracy); if the two lines were parallel then phi_1 = c phi_0 + d and Delta_i = -d would be constant on the first, contradicting the sign change; so they cross at a point p with Delta_i(p)=0, and since Delta_i is affine and changes sign along each line, p lies strictly inside both segments. Conversely a constant g_i keeps Delta_i of one sign on the segment. (c) a square with both coordinates non-constant is the directed 4-cycle, which has two sinks.
results.verification: Verified numerically on the two realised one-player games (crosscheck.py): 60 (face,coordinate) tests, 0 mismatches between 'g non-constant' and 'the two segments meet' (LP feasibility of the segment intersection).

results.name: gad:B2-min
results.statement: Call a pair (2-face F, Max coordinate c) forbidden when g_c restricted to F is exactly the split by the non-constant coordinate of F. B^2 has exactly four forbidden pairs, all on the face spanned by {x,alpha_1} at beta_1=0: coordinate alpha_2 at layers (alpha_2,beta_2)=(0,1) and (1,1), and coordinate beta_2 at layers (1,0) and (1,1). Hence in every nondegenerate stopping realisation of B^2 the Min best response is non-constant on each of those three 2-faces; in particular Vmin is nonempty. B^1 has no forbidden pair and is realised by a one-player game.
results.argument: gad:face applied to the outmap of B^2, enumerated over all 80 two-faces and all five coordinates. This gives a proof that B^2 needs Min vertices which is independent of Holt-Klee and which LOCALISES the obstruction, and it is exactly what made the construction findable.
results.verification: faces.py (enumeration). Independent census validation: over the 12640 AUSO classes of the 4-cube, all 6113 Holt-Klee classes have no forbidden pair; of the 6527 non-Holt-Klee classes 4365 have one and 2162 do not - so the test is implied by, and strictly weaker than, Holt-Klee. The height-7 class of prop:auso-seven has a forbidden pair, so gad:face re-proves cor:seven-two-player without Holt-Klee. Decisive measurement: the two best independent candidates of the free sequential-LP search (6 wrong incidences of 160, different seeds) both have tau constant on all three critical faces, and four of their six wrong incidences are EXACTLY the four forbidden pairs (diag.py).

results.name: gad:pi
results.statement: No affine functional of the value vectors of a one-player realisation of B^1 has the sign of the parity of the bottom-antipodal height; the same holds inside any layer of a realisation of B^2 on which the four strategies with beta_1=0 share a Min best response.
results.argument: On the face beta_1=0 the heights of B^1 are 0,1,2,3 at (x,alpha_1)=(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1), so the parity is the split by sigma_x, and g_x is non-constant there; apply gad:face(c). Since a Max row difference IS an affine functional of the value vector, this is precisely why the outer pair of a level-two realisation cannot read the inner parity without a Min vertex.
results.verification: Predicted and confirmed: a local search found 25 independent one-player realisations of B^1 and the parity separation is infeasible in every one (inner3c.py); for the two published realisations the Radon certificate is supported exactly on the four strategies with beta_1=0 (farkas.py), as the lemma predicts.

results.name: gad:precision
results.statement: Let G be nondegenerate stopping, alpha a Max vertex, and sigma_0,...,sigma_h a sequence with sigma_{t+1} = sigma_t[S_t] for nonempty sets S_t of strictly switchable vertices, along which alpha's incidence alternates. Then the sum over t=1..h-1 of |Delta_alpha(val_{sigma_t})| is at most 1, so the smallest margin is at most 1/(h-1), and G has at least log_2(h-1) average vertices. Corollary: a realisation of B(s) needs at least log_2(h(s)-1) average vertices; for the tower B^k (heights 3.2^k - 2) at least k+1, i.e. at least (m-1)/2 in dimension m = 2k+1.
results.argument: Write z_t = val_{sigma_t}, d_t = z_{t+1}-z_t >= 0 by lem:switch, and Delta_alpha = w.z + c with w = p^{alpha,1}-p^{alpha,0}, so ||w||_1 <= 2. Alternation gives |w.d_t| = |Delta(z_{t+1})| + |Delta(z_t)|, and summing, 2 sum_{t=1}^{h-1}|Delta(z_t)| <= sum_t |w|.d_t = |w|.(z_h - z_0) <= ||w||_1 <= 2. Finally Delta_alpha(val_sigma) is a difference of two entries of val_sigma, all multiples of 1/D for one integer D <= 2^{|Vavg|} (lem:denominator-sharp), and it is nonzero by nondegeneracy. The alternating sequence exists in B(s): take sigma_t = (v_t, alpha=0, beta=1) with v_t the bottom-antipodal walk of s, switching only the inner part s(v_t).
results.verification: Algebraic; consistent with both realised levels (level 1: 53 average vertices, log_2 3 = 1.6 required; level 2: 130 average vertices, log_2 9 = 3.2 required). This is the first size statement about the tower and it falls on the favourable side: the necessary precision grows only linearly in the level.

results.name: gad:xor (task (b): how the realised blow-up of the 2-cube translates)
results.statement: In the 100-vertex one-player game AP_m4_k0_den256_s200 realising B of the 2-cube (seed (3,2,0,1), translation vector the single inner coordinate e_1; the automorphism to natural coordinates is the permutation (0,1,3,2) composed with complementation of all four coordinates), with L the indicator of the layer (alpha,beta)=(0,0): (i) action 0 of the translated coordinate x_1 is a pure self-return (84/256 on itself, 21/256 to t_1), so val_sigma(x_1) = 21/172 whenever sigma_1 = 0; (ii) 256 Delta_1 = 7z_0 - 71z_1 + 133z_2 + 102z_3 - 21 is positive exactly on L, making val_sigma(x_1) a three-level signal (= 21/172 if sigma_1=0; < it if sigma_1=1, L=0; > it if sigma_1=1, L=1); (iii) 256 Delta_0 = 165z_1 + 4z_3 - 40z_0 - 121z_2 - 2, i.e. the comparison of that moving level with the threshold T = (40z_0+121z_2-4z_3+2)/165, and max_{L=0} T = 2497696403/23623057920 < 21/172 < 347482169/2787045602 = min_{L=1} T. Hence sign Delta_0 = NOT(sigma_1 XOR L): the layer term 121 z_2 carries the threshold across the pinned level and a single affine comparison realises the exclusive or with monotone readouts.
results.argument: This is the mechanism rem:blowup-measured left unanalysed: pinning by a self-returning action turns the translated coordinate's value into a three-level signal whose two extreme levels are the two states of the layer, and the other inner coordinate reads that signal against a threshold into which the layer enters with the opposite sign. Neither ingredient survives unchanged to inner dimension three: gad:B2-rows forbids the pinning at every Max vertex of a realisation of B^2, and where at inner dimension two the translated coordinate's incidence is constant off the layer, at inner dimension three it is (x AND alpha_1) XOR L, so its value carries a conjunction as well.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic (mech4.py, exactT.py): all sixteen value vectors, the sign pattern of Delta_1 ('------------++++', equal to L), the sign pattern of Delta_0 ('++--++--++----++', equal to NOT(sigma_1 XOR L)), the exact levels and the exact threshold bounds.

results.name: gad:B2-size (task (2): the size recurrence)
results.statement: The tower now has two realised levels: level 1, dimension 3, height 4, |C| = 3 (3 Max), denominator 2^6, N = 58; level 2, dimension 5, height 10, |C| = 6 (5 Max, 1 Min), denominator 2^9, N = 138. The increments are +2 Max vertices, +1 Min vertex and +3 bits of precision. A normal form on |C| controlled vertices with dyadic probabilities of denominator 2^d is realised by O(|C|^2 d) average vertices via the binary-expansion chains of def:damping/sec:fold, so the tower is polynomial (N = O(m^2) if the increments persist, N = O(m^3) in general) exactly when the precision is additive, and exponential when it is multiplicative.
results.argument: Two data points, not a recurrence. What IS proved is the lower bound of gad:precision: d_k >= k+1, so additive growth is necessary and the theorem leaves it possible. Neither denominator is known to be least; both come from a search. If the increments persist (|C_k| = 3k, d_k = 3k+3) the tower meets prop:auso-size's size clause and all-switches is exponential - a conditional statement about a pattern with two data points, not a theorem. A structural side measurement: the number of (2-face, coordinate) pairs forcing a non-constant Min response along the tower is 0, 4, 28, 136, 600 at levels 1..5 (dimensions 3,5,7,9,11) out of 6, 80, 672, 4608, 28160 two-faces - a shrinking fraction, but exponentially many, so the Min response map must be active across a constant fraction of the cube.
results.verification: Level 2 verified as above; level 1 is the published 58-vertex game; growth.py for the forbidden-pair counts.

gap: The third level, B^3 = B(B^2) - dimension 7, bottom-antipodal height 22 - is now the smallest open instance of the pivot, and with it the only question the tower leaves: whether one blow-up level can always be added at a constant additive cost in precision. Stated exactly: THERE IS A CONSTANT c SUCH THAT FOR EVERY LEVEL k THE ORIENTATION B^k IS THE IMPROVEMENT ORIENTATION OF A NONDEGENERATE STOPPING SSG WHOSE CONTROLLED PART HAS O(k) VERTICES AND ALL OF WHOSE FIRST-PASSAGE PROBABILITIES ARE DYADIC OF DENOMINATOR AT MOST 2^{ck}. Nothing here proves that, and nothing here refutes it: gad:precision proves the necessary c is at least 1, gad:B2-size measures c = 3 over the single step from level one to level two, and the construction at level two was found by a numerical programme rather than by a rule that visibly iterates.
next_steps: 1. Realise B^3 with the same machinery, which is now fully mechanical: run slp6.py at m=7 with the Min response prescribed to vary on the forbidden faces (there are 28 of them, faces.py lists them; the free-coordinate pairs are {x,alpha_1} and {x,beta_2}), then polish.py and build512.py. The only new ingredient needed is a good prescribed tau for 7 coordinates and probably two Min vertices; the level-two run took minutes of CPU once the tau was right. A third data point would turn gad:B2-size from a pattern into a recurrence. 2. Read off, from the 138-vertex normal form, the rule by which its rows encode the layer and the parity, and try to write it as a level-to-level transformation of normal forms rather than a search target - the theorems gad:readout, gad:mono, gad:face and gad:precision give exactly the four constraints such a rule must satisfy. 3. Extend gad:face to d-faces: the 2^d value vectors of a d-face whose strategies share a Min best response lie in a d-flat cut by d pairs of hyperplanes, so the induced orientation is realised by a d-dimensional arrangement; the d = 2 case already gives a local necessary condition strictly weaker than Holt-Klee, and d = 3 may separate more. 4. Check whether gad:precision can be sharpened by counting several alternating coordinates at once; a bound of the form |Vavg| >= h/poly would close the pivot negatively, and the present proof gives only log_2 h because the total variation of a substochastic row difference along a monotone chain is at most 2.

\subsection{What a game can read off its own values}
\label{sec:gadget}

This section is the constructive side of \Cref{rem:blowup-realise}: it isolates
the mechanism by which the realised blow-up at inner dimension two produces a
\emph{translated} sign pattern from monotone readouts, turns the remaining
obstacle into three statements about normal-form rows, and then realises the
second level. Throughout, $G$ is a stopping SSG in the harmonic normal form of
\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}: $C=\Vmax\cup\Vmin$, and each action $a$ at $v\in C$
carries the first-passage law $(p^{v,a},q^{v,a})$ of the average part onto $C$
and onto $t_1$, so that $V^a_v(z):=p^{v,a}\cdot z+q^{v,a}$ is the value of that
action when the value vector on $C$ is $z$.

\begin{definition}[The reduced rows]\label{gad:reduced}
For $v\in C$ and $a\in\{0,1\}$ put
\[
  \hat p^{v,a}_u:=\frac{p^{v,a}_u}{1-p^{v,a}_v}\ (u\ne v),\qquad
  \hat q^{v,a}:=\frac{q^{v,a}}{1-p^{v,a}_v},
\]
the first-passage law of action $a$ \emph{conditioned on leaving $v$} (the
stochastic complement of Meyer, from memory, unchecked against the source).
It is again substochastic: $\sum_{u\ne v}\hat p^{v,a}_u+\hat q^{v,a}\le1$.
Write $A_v(y):=\hat p^{v,0}\cdot y+\hat q^{v,0}$ and
$B_v(y):=\hat p^{v,1}\cdot y+\hat q^{v,1}$ for $y\in\mathbb R^{C\setminus\{v\}}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The readout identity]\label{gad:readout}
Let $G$ be stopping, $x_i\in\Vmax$, $\sigma$ a Max strategy and
$y:=\val_\sigma|_{C\setminus\{x_i\}}$. Then
\[
  \val_\sigma(x_i)=\begin{cases}A_i(y),&\sigma_i=0,\\ B_i(y),&\sigma_i=1,\end{cases}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \operatorname{sign}\Delta_i(\val_\sigma)=\operatorname{sign}\bigl(B_i(y)-A_i(y)\bigr),
\]
where $\Delta_i:=V^1_i-V^0_i$. Consequently $\val_\sigma(x_i)$ takes three
levels relative to the reference $A_i(y)$: it equals it when $\sigma_i=0$,
exceeds it exactly when $\sigma_i=1$ and $i$ is not switchable at $\sigma$, and
falls below it exactly when $\sigma_i=1$ and $i$ is switchable. In particular
the state of $x_i$ is visible in the value vector only through the conjunction
of $\sigma_i$ with the incidence of $x_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
With $t:=\val_\sigma(x_i)$ we have $t=V^{\sigma_i}_i(y,t)=p^{i,\sigma_i}_it+
\sum_{u\ne i}p^{i,\sigma_i}_uy_u+q^{i,\sigma_i}$, and $p^{i,\sigma_i}_i<1$
because $G$ is stopping, so $t=A_i(y)$ or $B_i(y)$ as claimed. If $\sigma_i=0$
then $V^0_i(y,t)=t=A_i(y)$ and
$\Delta_i=V^1_i(y,A_i)-A_i=(1-p^{i,1}_i)\,(B_i(y)-A_i(y))$; if $\sigma_i=1$ then
$\Delta_i=B_i(y)-V^0_i(y,B_i)=(1-p^{i,0}_i)\,(B_i(y)-A_i(y))$. Both prefactors
are positive. The three levels are the two displayed formulas together with
\Cref{def:improvement-uso}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Comparable rows cannot turn]\label{gad:mono}
Let $G$ be nondegenerate stopping with improvement orientation $s_G$, and let
$\preceq$ be the reachability preorder of $s_G$ (so $\sigma\preceq\sigma'$ when
a directed path of $s_G$ runs from $\sigma$ to $\sigma'$; by \Cref{lem:switch}
$\val_\sigma\le\val_{\sigma'}$ componentwise then). Fix $x_i\in\Vmax$ and write
$g_i(\sigma)=+$ when the $i$-edge at $\sigma$ points from $\sigma_i=0$ to
$\sigma_i=1$. If $\hat p^{i,1}\ge\hat p^{i,0}$ and $\hat q^{i,1}\ge\hat q^{i,0}$
then $\{g_i=+\}$ is up-closed for $\preceq$; if the reverse inequalities hold it
is down-closed. Hence if $\{g_i=+\}$ is neither up- nor down-closed, the two
reduced rows of $x_i$ are incomparable.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{gad:readout}, $g_i(\sigma)$ is the sign of $(B_i-A_i)(\val_\sigma)$,
an affine functional of the value vector whose coefficients are
$\hat p^{i,1}-\hat p^{i,0}$. Under the stated inequalities it is nondecreasing,
and $\val$ is nondecreasing along $\preceq$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Every vertex of a level-two realisation must turn]\label{gad:B2-rows}
In every nondegenerate stopping SSG whose improvement orientation is
$B^2:=B(B(\text{$1$-cube}))$ of \Cref{thm:blowup} --- the $5$-cube orientation
of bottom-antipodal height $10$ with outmap
$(7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6,24,9,27,14,31,28,29,10,16,25,19,30,23,20,21,26,8,17,11,22,15,12,13,18)$
--- the two reduced rows of \emph{each} of the five Max vertices are
incomparable. In particular no Max vertex may have an action that goes straight
to the sinks, nor an action that returns only to itself and the sinks. For
$B^1=B(\text{$1$-cube})$, by contrast, only the coordinate $\beta_1$ needs
incomparable rows: $\{g=+\}$ is down-closed at the seed coordinate and at
$\alpha_1$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
A finite check on the outmap. For each of the five coordinates $c$ the
orientation contains a directed edge along which $g_c$ passes from $+$ to $-$
and another along which it passes from $-$ to $+$; with the coordinates
numbered $x,\alpha_1,\beta_1,\alpha_2,\beta_2$ (bits $0,\dots,4$) the witnesses
are $0\to4$ and $8\to0$ for $x$; $0\to1$ and $8\to0$ for $\alpha_1$;
$2\to3$ and $3\to1$ for $\beta_1$; $17\to16$ and $18\to19$ for $\alpha_2$;
$8\to0$ and $9\to8$ for $\beta_2$. For $B^1$ the same enumeration finds no
$+\to-$ edge for $x$ and none for $\alpha_1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{gad:B2-rows-remark}
\Cref{gad:B2-rows} removes the ansatz that realises the level-one blow-up and
that the realised blow-up of the $2$-cube uses at its translated coordinate
(\Cref{gad:xor} below): there, one action of the translated vertex is a pure
self-return, which pins its value to a constant and makes the whole
configuration transparent. At level two no vertex may be pinned in that way.
\end{remark}

\subsection{A two-face test for the Min vertices}

\begin{lemma}[The crossing lemma]\label{gad:face}
Let $G$ be a nondegenerate stopping SSG, let $F$ be a $2$-face of the Max cube
spanned by the coordinates $i\ne j$, and suppose some single Min strategy
$\tau$ is optimal against all four Max strategies of $F$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] the four value vectors lie in an affine subspace of dimension~$2$;
\item[(b)] inside it the segment joining the two values with $\sigma_i=0$ and
the segment joining the two with $\sigma_i=1$ have a common point if and only
if $g_i$ is non-constant on $F$;
\item[(c)] the unique-sink axiom makes at most one of $g_i,g_j$ non-constant on
$F$; and if $g_i$ is the non-constant one, then no affine functional of the
value vector separates $\{\sigma\in F:\sigma_i=0\}$ from
$\{\sigma\in F:\sigma_i=1\}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) $\val_\sigma$ is the unique solution of the $|C|$ equations
$z_v=V^{\sigma_v}_v(z)$ $(v\in\Vmax)$, $z_y=V^{\tau_y}_y(z)$ $(y\in\Vmin)$; a
family of $|C|$ hyperplanes in $\mathbb R^{C}$ with a unique common point is
independent, so the $|C|-2$ of them shared by the four strategies of $F$ meet
in a plane $\Pi$ of dimension exactly $2$, and the four values lie in $\Pi$.

(b) Put $\varphi_0(z):=z_i-V^0_i(z)$ and $\varphi_1(z):=z_i-V^1_i(z)$, so that
$\Delta_i=\varphi_0-\varphi_1$, the two values with $\sigma_i=0$ lie on
$\ell_0:=\{\varphi_0=0\}\cap\Pi$ and the two with $\sigma_i=1$ on
$\ell_1:=\{\varphi_1=0\}\cap\Pi$. Neither $\varphi_0$ nor $\varphi_1$ is
constant on $\Pi$: if $\varphi_0$ were, it would vanish identically on $\Pi$
(it vanishes at two points of $\Pi$), and then at the two points with
$\sigma_i=1$ both $\varphi_0$ and $\varphi_1$ would vanish, forcing
$\Delta_i=0$ there against nondegeneracy; symmetrically for $\varphi_1$. So
$\ell_0,\ell_1$ are lines. If they were parallel, the linear parts of
$\varphi_0,\varphi_1$ on $\Pi$ would be proportional, $\varphi_1=c\varphi_0+d$
with $c\ne0$, and then $\Delta_i=-d$ would be constant on $\ell_0$; so
$g_i$ non-constant on $F$ forces $\ell_0$ and $\ell_1$ to meet, and their
intersection point $p$ satisfies $\varphi_0(p)=\varphi_1(p)=0$, i.e.
$\Delta_i(p)=0$. Since $\Delta_i$ is affine and changes sign between the two
points of $\ell_0$, its unique zero on $\ell_0$ --- which is $p$ --- lies
strictly between them, and likewise on $\ell_1$: the two segments meet at $p$.
Conversely if $g_i$ is constant on $F$ then $\Delta_i$ has one sign on the whole
$\ell_0$-segment, so it does not vanish there and the segments are disjoint.

(c) A square whose two coordinates both have a non-constant $g$ is the directed
$4$-cycle, which has two sinks, so it is not a unique sink orientation; the
faces of an improvement orientation are (\Cref{prop:allsw-auso}). The last
clause is (b) together with the separation theorem.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Where the Min vertices of a level-two realisation must
act]\label{gad:B2-min}
Call a pair (a $2$-face $F$, a Max coordinate $c$) \emph{forbidden} for an
orientation when $g_c$ restricted to $F$ is exactly the split by the
non-constant coordinate of $F$. For $B^2$ there are exactly four forbidden
pairs, all on the face spanned by $\{x,\alpha_1\}$ at $\beta_1=0$: the
coordinate $\alpha_2$ at the layers $(\alpha_2,\beta_2)=(0,1)$ and $(1,1)$, and
the coordinate $\beta_2$ at the layers $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$. Hence in every
nondegenerate stopping realisation of $B^2$ the Min best response is
non-constant on each of the three $2$-faces $\{x,\alpha_1\}$ at $\beta_1=0$ and
$(\alpha_2,\beta_2)\ne(0,0)$; in particular $\Vmin\ne\emptyset$. The
orientation $B^1$ has no forbidden pair, and it is realised by a one-player
game.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}\label{gad:face-census}
The forbidden-pair test is a local necessary condition for one-player
realisability, and it is implied by, but strictly weaker than, Holt--Klee. Over
the $12640$ isomorphism classes of AUSOs of the $4$-cube
(\Cref{prop:auso-census}): all $6113$ Holt--Klee classes have no forbidden pair;
of the $6527$ non-Holt--Klee classes, $4365$ have one and $2162$ do not. The
height-$7$ class of \Cref{prop:auso-seven} has a forbidden pair, so
\Cref{gad:face} re-proves \Cref{cor:seven-two-player} without Holt--Klee, and
localises the obstruction to a single $2$-face. Along the tower
$B^k$ of \Cref{thm:blowup} the numbers of forbidden pairs are
$0,4,28,136,600$ at $k=1,\dots,5$ (dimensions $3,5,7,9,11$), out of
$6,80,672,4608,28160$ two-faces.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[The parity is not readable from the Max rows]\label{gad:pi}
Let $G$ be a nondegenerate stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ whose
improvement orientation is $B^1$, and let $\pi(v)$ be the parity of the
bottom-antipodal height of $v$ in $B^1$. Then no affine functional of the value
vector has sign $\pi$: the eight value vectors are not separated by $\pi$. The
same holds inside any single layer of a realisation of $B^2$ on which the four
strategies with $\beta_1=0$ share a Min best response.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
On the face $\beta_1=0$ the heights of $B^1$ are $0,1,2,3$ at
$(x,\alpha_1)=(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)$, so $\pi$ is the split by $\sigma_x$;
and $g_x$ is non-constant on that face ($-$ at $\alpha_1=0$, $+$ at
$\alpha_1=1$). Apply \Cref{gad:face}(c) with the empty Min strategy.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{gad:pi-measured}
\Cref{gad:pi} is why the outer coordinate of a level-two realisation cannot
read the inner parity through a Max row difference alone: an affine functional
of the value vector is exactly what a Max row difference is. We found $25$
independent one-player realisations of $B^1$ by local search; in every one the
parity separation is infeasible, and for the two published realisations the
Farkas certificate is supported exactly on the four strategies with
$\beta_1=0$, as \Cref{gad:pi} predicts. A Min vertex escapes the lemma:
clipping the value of $x$ from above at a level between $A_x$ and
$A_x+\Delta_x$ moves one of the four points off the plane $\Pi$, and then the
separation becomes feasible --- this is the $\min(\theta,x)$ device of
\Cref{rem:blowup-realise}, and \Cref{gad:face} says where it has to be placed.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The precision a blow-up needs}

\begin{theorem}[Alternation costs bits]\label{gad:precision}
Let $G$ be a nondegenerate stopping SSG, $\alpha\in\Vmax$, and let
$\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_h$ be Max strategies with $\sigma_{t+1}=\sigma_t[S_t]$
for nonempty sets $S_t$ of vertices strictly switchable at $\sigma_t$, and
suppose the incidence of $\alpha$ alternates,
$\operatorname{sign}\Delta_\alpha(\val_{\sigma_t})=(-1)^t$. Then
\[
  \sum_{t=1}^{h-1}\bigl|\Delta_\alpha(\val_{\sigma_t})\bigr|\;\le\;1,
  \qquad\text{so}\qquad \min_t\bigl|\Delta_\alpha(\val_{\sigma_t})\bigr|\le\frac1{h-1},
\]
and therefore $|\Vavg|\ge\log_2(h-1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $z_t:=\val_{\sigma_t}|_C\in[0,1]^C$ and $d_t:=z_{t+1}-z_t$, which is
$\ge0$ by \Cref{lem:switch}. Also $\Delta_\alpha(z)=w\cdot z+c$ with
$w=p^{\alpha,1}-p^{\alpha,0}$, so $\|w\|_1\le2$. Alternation gives
$|w\cdot d_t|=|\Delta_\alpha(z_{t+1})-\Delta_\alpha(z_t)|
=|\Delta_\alpha(z_{t+1})|+|\Delta_\alpha(z_t)|$, whence
\[
 2\sum_{t=1}^{h-1}|\Delta_\alpha(z_t)|\;\le\;\sum_{t=0}^{h-1}|w\cdot d_t|
 \;\le\;\sum_{t=0}^{h-1}|w|\cdot d_t\;=\;|w|\cdot(z_h-z_0)\;\le\;\|w\|_1\;\le\;2 .
\]
Finally $\Delta_\alpha(\val_\sigma)=\val_\sigma(\alpha^{(1)})-\val_\sigma(\alpha^{(0)})$
is a difference of two entries of $\val_\sigma$, and by
\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp} all entries of $\val_\sigma$ are multiples of
$1/D$ for one integer $D\le2^{|\Vavg|}$; nondegeneracy makes the difference
nonzero, so $1/D\le1/(h-1)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{gad:precision-blowup}
A nondegenerate stopping SSG realising $B(s)$ --- in which the outer coordinate
$\alpha$ has $g_\alpha(\sigma)=+$ exactly when $\beta=1$ and the inner height
$h(v)$ is odd --- has at least $\log_2(h(s)-1)$ average vertices. For the tower
$B^k$ of \Cref{thm:blowup}, whose heights are $h_k=3\cdot2^{k}-2$, a
realisation at level $k$ needs at least $k+1$ average vertices, that is at
least $(m-1)/2$ in dimension $m=2k+1$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Take $\sigma_t=(v_t,\alpha{=}0,\beta{=}1)$ with $v_0,\dots,v_h$ the
bottom-antipodal walk of $s$ from a vertex of maximal height; at each step the
switched set is the inner part $s(v_t)$ of the outmap of $B(s)$ at $\sigma_t$,
a nonempty set of strictly switchable vertices, and $h(v_t)$ drops by one, so
the incidence of $\alpha$ alternates. Apply \Cref{gad:precision}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The size recurrence]\label{gad:size}
\Cref{gad:precision-blowup} is the first size statement about the tower, and it
falls on the favourable side. One level of \Cref{thm:blowup} adds two Max
vertices and, by \Cref{gad:B2-min}, at least one Min vertex, so
$|C_{k+1}|=|C_k|+O(1)$; a normal form on $|C|$ controlled vertices with all
probabilities dyadic of denominator $2^d$ is realised by
$O(|C|^2d)$ average vertices through the binary-expansion chains of
\Cref{def:damping} and \Cref{sec:fold}. So the whole tower is polynomial
exactly when the precision is additive, $d_{k+1}=d_k+O(1)$, and exponential
when it is multiplicative. \Cref{gad:precision-blowup} shows $d_k\ge k+1$:
additive growth is \emph{necessary}, and the theorem leaves it possible.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The mechanism at inner dimension two}

\begin{proposition}[How the realised blow-up of the $2$-cube
translates]\label{gad:xor}
Let $H$ be the nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG on $100$ vertices of
\Cref{rem:blowup-measured} realising $B$ of the $2$-cube, in the harmonic
normal form with Max vertices $x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3$ and denominator $256$:
\[
 \begin{array}{r@{\quad}l@{\qquad}l}
  x_0: & (51,0,121,0\,|\,4) & (11,165,0,4\,|\,2)\\
  x_1: & (0,84,0,0\,|\,21) & (7,13,133,102\,|\,0)\\
  x_2: & (94,0,160,0\,|\,1) & (1,12,70,171\,|\,0)\\
  x_3: & (19,94,8,114\,|\,0) & (10,38,97,102\,|\,2),
 \end{array}
\]
the two rows of each vertex being $(p\,|\,q)$ over the targets
$(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3\,|\,t_1)$. Identify $x_0,x_1$ with the two inner
coordinates, $x_2$ with $\beta$ and $x_3$ with $\alpha$, all four actions
exchanged; the seed is the $2$-cube orientation $(3,2,0,1)$ and the translation
vector of \Cref{thm:blowup} is the single inner coordinate $e_1$. Write $L$ for
the indicator of the layer $(\alpha,\beta)=(0,0)$, that is of
$\sigma_2=\sigma_3=1$ in the game's coordinates. Then, in exact arithmetic:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] the action $0$ of $x_1$ is a pure self-return, so
$\val_\sigma(x_1)=\tfrac{21}{172}$ whenever $\sigma_1=0$;
\item[(ii)] $256\,\Delta_1=7z_0-71z_1+133z_2+102z_3-21$ is positive exactly on
the four strategies with $L=1$; with (i) and \Cref{gad:readout} this makes
$\val_\sigma(x_1)$ a three-level signal,
\[
  \val_\sigma(x_1)\;\begin{cases}=\tfrac{21}{172},&\sigma_1=0,\\
  <\tfrac{21}{172},&\sigma_1=1,\ L=0,\\ >\tfrac{21}{172},&\sigma_1=1,\ L=1;\end{cases}
\]
\item[(iii)] $256\,\Delta_0=165z_1+4z_3-40z_0-121z_2-2$, that is the comparison
of the moving level $z_1$ with the threshold
$T:=(40z_0+121z_2-4z_3+2)/165$, and
$\max_{L=0}T=\tfrac{2497696403}{23623057920}<\tfrac{21}{172}
<\tfrac{347482169}{2787045602}=\min_{L=1}T$ --- the layer term $121z_2$ carries
the threshold across the pinned level. Hence
$\operatorname{sign}\Delta_0=+$ exactly when $\sigma_1\oplus L=0$: the inner
coordinate $x_0$ compares its options as it would at the flipped $\sigma_1$
precisely on the layer $(0,0)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}\label{gad:xor-transfer}
\Cref{gad:xor} is the whole of \Cref{rem:blowup-measured}'s ``how that game
does it''. Two ingredients: the translated coordinate is \emph{pinned} by a
self-returning action, so its value is a three-level signal whose two extreme
levels are the two states of the layer; and the other inner coordinate
compares that signal against a threshold into which the layer enters with the
opposite sign, so that a single affine comparison realises the exclusive or.
Neither ingredient survives to inner dimension three unchanged.
\Cref{gad:B2-rows} forbids the pinning at every Max vertex of a realisation of
$B^2$; and where at inner dimension two the translated coordinate's incidence
was constant off the layer $(0,0)$ --- so that its value carried exactly
$\sigma_j\wedge L$ --- at inner dimension three the incidence of the translated
coordinate $\beta_1$ is $(x\wedge\alpha_1)\oplus L$, so its value carries a
conjunction as well, and the two remaining inner coordinates must read
$\beta_1\oplus L$ from it. Finally \Cref{gad:pi} says the outer pair cannot
read the inner parity at all without a Min vertex, and \Cref{gad:B2-min} says
exactly which two-faces that Min vertex must break.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The second level is realised}

\begin{theorem}[The second blow-up level is realised, on $138$ vertices]\label{gad:B2}
Let $G^{\flat}$ be the SSG with five Max vertices $c_1,\dots,c_5$, one Min
vertex $c_6$ and the harmonic normal form below, each action being given as its
first-passage law over the targets $(c_1,\dots,c_6\mid t_1)$ in multiples of
$\tfrac1{512}$, the remaining mass going to $t_0$:
\[
 \begin{array}{r@{\quad}l@{\qquad}l}
  c_1: & (12,461,36,0,0,0\mid 0)  & (276,0,0,0,127,0\mid 47)\\
  c_2: & (0,0,509,0,0,0\mid 0)    & (0,83,0,0,320,0\mid 12)\\
  c_3: & (0,0,0,0,0,460\mid 43)   & (267,187,0,0,56,0\mid 0)\\

Every row sums to at most $511$, so every action leaks to $t_0$. Realising the

 s_{G^{\flat}}=B^2=(7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6,24,9,27,14,31,28,29,10,
 16,25,19,30,23,20,21,26,8,17,11,22,15,12,13,18),

an acyclic unique sink orientation of the $5$-cube whose bottom-antipodal

\[
 12\to19\to13\to17\to8\to16\to0\to7\to1\to5\to4 ,
\]
switching in turn
$\{c_1,\dots,c_5\},\{c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5\},\{c_3,c_4,c_5\},\{c_1,c_4,c_5\},
\{c_4,c_5\},\{c_5\},\{c_1,c_2,c_3\},\{c_2,c_3\},\{c_3\},\{c_1\}$.
The orientation is not Holt--Klee, so by \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp} the Min vertex
is necessary; and the Min best response is non-constant on each of the three
$2$-faces named in \Cref{gad:B2-min}, as it must be.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All assertions are finite exact computations, carried out twice: once on the
normal form and once on the built game, whose value vectors were also
cross-checked against an independent elimination. The greatest trap of the game
is empty, so it is stopping (\Cref{lem:trapchar}); every non-sink has
out-degree two. For each of the $32$ Max strategies the value $\val_\sigma$ was
computed as the componentwise minimum over both positional Min strategies of the
two pair values --- never by policy iteration --- and checked to be a fixed
point of $T_\sigma$. None of the $160$ incidences is tied, so $G^{\flat}$ is
nondegenerate in the sense of \Cref{def:improvement-uso}. The strictly
switchable sets are the outmap displayed; it satisfies the Szab\'o--Welzl
condition on all $\binom{32}{2}$ pairs and orients the $5$-cube acyclically.
Holt--Klee fails, by the unit vertex-capacity maximum-flow test of
\Cref{cor:seven-two-player}'s kind run on every face. Along the run the value
vector increases at every one of the $136$ non-sink vertices at every round, as
\Cref{lem:switch} requires.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What made it findable]\label{gad:B2-how}
Blind search over normal forms does not find this game: the annealers of the
present route stall at $18$--$26$ wrong incidences of $160$, and the
round-fourteen evolution strategy with the exact LP over the payoff column
stalls likewise. Two changes found it. The first is a \emph{sequential linear
programme}: for a fixed Min response the value vector is
$z_\sigma=(I-P_\sigma)^{-1}Q_\sigma$, so every improvement margin has an exact
first-order expansion in the rows, and one LP per iteration minimises the total
shortfall of the $160$ margins over a trust region. The second is
\Cref{gad:B2-min}: run with the Min response recomputed as a best response, the
programme converges to candidates with six wrong incidences whose Min response
is \emph{constant} on the three critical $2$-faces, and four of the six wrong
incidences are exactly the four forbidden pairs --- the residue of the search is
the theorem. Prescribing a Min response that varies on those faces, and imposing
its optimality as explicit constraints, makes the programme converge. One Min
vertex suffices, fewer than the two or three the earlier searches assumed. The
prescribed response used is $\tau=1$ exactly when the first two Max coordinates
are both~$1$.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The measured recurrence]\label{gad:B2-size}
With \Cref{gad:B2} the tower of \Cref{thm:blowup} has two realised levels:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c}
  \text{level }k & \dim m & \text{height} & |C| & \text{denominator} & N\\\hline
  1 & 3 & 4  & 3 \text{ (3 Max)}          & 2^{6} & 58\\
  2 & 5 & 10 & 6 \text{ (5 Max, 1 Min)}   & 2^{9} & 138
 \end{array}
\]
so the increments are $+2$ Max vertices, $+1$ Min vertex and $+3$ bits of
precision. This is the additive regime of \Cref{gad:size}: two levels do not
make a recurrence, but they are the first evidence that the precision does not
have to square, and \Cref{gad:precision-blowup} says it cannot grow more slowly
than one bit per level. Neither denominator is known to be least; both come
from a search. If the increments persist --- $|C_k|=3k$, $d_k=3k+3$ --- the
tower is realised on $N=O(k^{2})=O(m^{2})$ vertices, and then
\Cref{prop:auso-size}'s size clause is met and all-switches is exponential.
That is a conditional statement about a pattern with two data points; it is not
a theorem, and the third level is now the smallest open instance.
\end{remark}
